Rashi on Chullin 32a:10:1.english: Standing - [The other animal] is already here, lacking only being thrown down to the ground [to be slaughtered].

Rashi on Chullin 32a:10:2.hebrew: איכא - בין רבי חנינא לרבי יוחנן: רבי יוחנן משער בשחיטה לחודה, ורבי חנינא בעי הטלה ושחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:10:2.english: There is [a difference] - Between Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Yochanan: Rabbi Yochanan estimates [the time] by the slaughtering alone, while Rabbi Chanina requires [the time for] bringing [the animal] and slaughtering.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:11:1.hebrew: דקה לדקה - לשהיית בהמה דקה משערינן בכדי שחיטת בהמה דקה דכוותה. ואף על גב דרב ורבי יוחנן הלכה כרבי יוחנן, כיון דקים ליה רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא בשיטתיה דרב דאמר דקה לדקה וגסה לגסה, ממילא שמעינן ועוף לעוף, ועבדינן לחומרא:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:11:1.english: A small animal to a small animal - For a delay [in slaughtering] a small animal (sheep or goat), we estimate [the maximum permissible delay] by the time it takes to slaughter a comparable small animal. And even though [when] Rav and Rabbi Yochanan [disagree] the halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan, since it is known that Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina follows Rav's opinion, who said "small to small and large to large," we may infer from this on our own also "fowl to fowl," and we act stringently.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:12:1.hebrew: בסכין רעה - שאין חידודה חותך יפה:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:12:1.english: With a bad knife - [Meaning] one whose sharpness does not cut well.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:12:2.hebrew: אפילו כל היום כולו - ומאריך ושוהה בשחיטה אחת:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:12:2.english: Even the entire day - Meaning he prolongs and delays a single act of slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:12:3.hebrew: כשרה - הואיל וכל שעה הוא מוליך ומביא, ולא הפסיק בשחיטתו:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:12:3.english: It is valid - Since the whole time he was moving [the knife] back and forth, and he did not interrupt his slaughtering.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:13:1.hebrew: שהיות מהו שיצטרפו - הפסיק ב' ושלש פעמים בשחיטה אחת, ושהה בין שלשתן כדי שיעור שלם:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:13:1.english: Pauses - what is [the law] as to whether they combine - [The case is where] he paused two or three times during a single act of slaughtering, and the time he waited between the three [pauses], combined, equals the full measure [of an invalidating pause].

Rashi on Chullin 32a:14:1.hebrew: מדידיה - השוחט בסכין רעה, אלמא לא מצטרפי, דקא ס"ד, ואפילו הפסיק קאמר, אלא שלא שהה בפעם אחת כשיעור:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:14:1.english: From his own [statement] - [Rava's own words:] "One who slaughters with a bad knife" [is valid even the whole day, provided he did not pause] - this shows that [interruptions] do not combine. For you might have thought that even though it says he "interrupted" [many times over the course of the day, these would combine to invalidate the slaughter] - rather, [the disqualification is only] that he did not pause the full requisite duration in one single [continuous] stretch.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:14:2.english: There, where he did not pause - Not at all.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:15:1.hebrew: במיעוט סימנים - שחט הרוב, ושהה במיעוט האחרון, וגמר שחיטתו:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:15:1.english: During the minority of the [two] simanim [i.e., the windpipe and gullet] - [Meaning:] He slaughtered the majority [of one of the simanim], then paused during [the cutting of] the remaining minority, and [then] completed his slaughtering.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:15:2.hebrew: מהו - מי אמרינן כיון דעבד ליה רובא אתכשר, או דלמא כיון דהדר וגמרה כולה חדא שחיטה היא:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:15:2.english: What is [the halakha]? - Do we say that since he performed the majority of it, it is rendered fit? Or perhaps, since he went back and completed the whole thing, it is [regarded as] one [continuous] act of slaughtering?

Rashi on Chullin 32a:15:3.hebrew: תיקו - ולחומרא. ובמיעוט קמא, אי דגרגרת - לאו מידי עביד ולא שהייה היא, ואי דוושט - דנקובתו במשהו מיטרפא, ממה נפשך, דהא כיון דשהה אזיל ליה מעשה קמא, והוה ליה נקב בעלמא וטרפה. ונראה, דהשוחט רוב סימנין והשליך מידו, והעוף שוהה למות, אסור לחזור ולחתוך המיעוט בתורת שחיטה, דמוטב שיכה על הצואר בסכין, או ימתין עד שימות:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:15:3.english: Let it stand [undecided] - and [we rule] stringently. And regarding the first [case of a] minority [that was cut] - if it was of the windpipe, it accomplishes nothing and is not [considered] a pause; and if it was of the gullet - since a puncture of it, however slight, renders [the animal] tereifah - either way [it is tereifah], for since he paused, the first act is lost, and it becomes a mere puncture, and it is tereifah. And it seems that one who slaughtered the majority of the organs and cast [the knife] from his hand, and the bird lingers before dying, is forbidden to go back and cut the remaining minority as an act of ritual slaughter, for it is better that he strike it on the neck with the knife, or wait until it dies.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:16:1.english: The time it takes for a Sage to inspect - [Meaning,] examination of the knife.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:16:2.hebrew: לשיעורין - פעמים דחכם רחוק, ופעמים קרוב:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:16:2.english: In stages [with pauses] - Sometimes the Sage is far away, and sometimes he is near.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:16:3.hebrew: טבח חכם - שזה השוחט, חכם הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:16:3.english: A wise slaughterer - Meaning that this slaughterer is wise.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:17:1.hebrew: ופסק את הגרגרת - היינו עיקור, ובבהמה קאי:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:17:1.english: And severed the trachea - This means he tore it out [rather than cutting it], and [the mishna] is speaking of an animal.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:17:2.english: Beneath the second [siman] - Between the [first] simon and the neck.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:17:3.english: And he severed it - From below to above.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:17:4.english: Yishvav - This is the name of a sage, and so it appears in Chronicles (I 24) regarding the priestly divisions.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:1:1.hebrew: נשחטה בהמה אחרת עמה - בלא מתכוין:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:1:1.english: Another animal was slaughtered with it - Unintentionally.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:1:2.hebrew: לרבי נתן - דמכשיר שחיטת חולין בלא כוונה, בהמה כשרה ופרה פסולה. ואע"ג דשלא בכוונה לא מסח דעתיה ולא מיקרי מתעסק במלאכה אחרת, הואיל ושחיטתו כשרה, מיפסלא משום "ושחט אותה" ולא אותה וחבירתה:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:1:2.english: According to Rabbi Natan - Who deems valid the slaughter of a non-sacred animal performed without special intent: the [other] animal is kosher, but the [red] heifer is invalid. And even though it was without intent, he did not divert his mind [from the slaughtering], and he is not regarded as occupied with a different task, since his slaughtering is otherwise valid. [Nevertheless,] it is disqualified on account of [the verse] "and he shall slaughter it" - it, and not it together with its fellow.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:1:3.hebrew: לרבנן פרה כשרה - דהא שחיטת בהמת חולין לאו שחיטה היא, ומשום מלאכה ליכא למיפסל, דשלא במתכוין לא מיקרי עוסק במלאכה אחרת, דטעמא דמלאכה אחרת משום דמסח דעתיה מפרה הוא, והיכא דלא איכוין למלאכה אחרת ליכא היסח הדעת. והכי אמרינן לקמן נחתכה דלעת עמה דברי הכל כשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:1:3.english: According to the Rabbis, the cow is valid - For slaughtering a non-sacred animal is not [considered] slaughter [for this purpose], and [the cow] cannot be disqualified on account of [performing] another labor, since doing something unintentionally is not called "engaging in another labor." For the reason that [performing] another labor [disqualifies the cow] is that it [shows] his mind was diverted from the cow; and where he did not intend to perform another labor, there is no diversion of the mind. And so we say further on: if a gourd was cut along with it, all agree that it is valid.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:2:1.hebrew: פשיטא - אכתי לא שמעינן דכל העוסקים בפרה פוסלין אותה במלאכה:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:2:1.english: Obviously - [The Gemara asks this because] we have not yet heard that all who are engaged in [the work of preparing] the [red] heifer disqualify it through [other, unrelated] labor.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:2:2.hebrew: נשחטה בהמה אחרת לר' נתן איצטריכא ליה - דכיון דמלאכה לא מיקריא שלא בכוונה, כדאמרינן לקמן "נחתכה דלעת עמה דברי הכל כשרה", משום שחיטת חבירתה נמי, אע"ג דשחיטה שלא בכוונה שמה שחיטה, הוה אמינא לא תפסול, ד"ושחט אותה" משמע ולא אותה וחבירתה, והיכי דמי, כגון ששחט שתי פרות אדומות בהדי הדדי:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:2:2.english: "Another animal was slaughtered" - for Rabbi Natan this was necessary [to teach] - Since an unintentional act is not termed "labor," as we say below: "If a gourd was cut along with it, all agree it is valid" - so too here, because of the slaughtering of its companion animal, even though an unintentional slaughtering is [nonetheless] called slaughtering, one might have thought it would not disqualify [the red heifer], since [the verse] "and he shall slaughter it" implies it alone, and not it together with its companion. And what is the case? For example, where he slaughtered two red heifers together.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:2:3.hebrew: קמ"ל - דחולין נמי משמע, אבל רישא דנתכוין לאחרת לא איצטריכא, דנהי נמי דאותה וחבירתה משמע שתי פרות אדומות, מיהו כיון דנתכוין למלאכה אחרת מיפסלא משום היסח הדעת, דלא גרעה מחתיכת דלעת:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:2:3.english: He teaches us - That a non-sacred animal [slaughtered together with it unintentionally] is also included [in the disqualification]. But the first case, where he intended [to perform] another [act while slaughtering], did not need to be taught, for although "it and its counterpart" implies [specifically] two red heifers, nevertheless, since he intended a different task, it is disqualified on account of a lapse of attention, for it is no less [disqualifying] than [intentionally] cutting a gourd [together with it].

Rashi on Chullin 32a:3:1.hebrew: חתך דלעת עמה דברי הכל פסולה - דהא מלאכה היא:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:3:1.english: If he cut a gourd along with it, all agree it is unfit - Since that is [also] labor.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:3:2.hebrew: נחתכה דלעת עמה דברי הכל כשרה - דשלא בכוונה לא מיקרי עוסק במלאכה, ורישא לרבי נתן טעמא דכתיב ושחט אותה ולא חבירתה עמה, ושלא בכוונה נמי שמה שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:3:2.english: If a gourd was cut along with it, all agree it is valid - Since it was unintentional, it is not called "engaged in [another] task." And [as for] the first clause [where another animal was slaughtered along with it], according to Rabbi Natan the reason is that it is written, "and he shall slaughter it" - it, and not its fellow along with it. And even unintentionally, this is nonetheless called slaughtering.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:4:1.hebrew: נפלה סכין והגביהה - ושהה בהגבהה זו:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:4:1.english: If the knife fell and he picked it up - And he delayed [in the slaughtering] during this picking up.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:4:3.english: Or he sharpened the knife - Before the slaughtering.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:4:4.hebrew: ועף - נתייגע וכשהתחיל לשחוט לא היה בו כח, ופסק שחיטתו, ובא חבירו ושחט:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:4:4.english: And he became weary - He grew tired, and when he began to slaughter he did not have the strength, so he stopped his slaughtering, and his fellow came and slaughtered.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:4:5.english: As long as it takes for an examination - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:5:1.english: What is [the meaning of] "as long as it takes to slaughter"? Rav said: As long as it takes to slaughter another animal - And do not say that it means only as long as it takes him to finish his own slaughtering, and no more.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:6:1.hebrew: בהמה לבהמה ועוף לעוף - כדי שחיטת בהמה אחרת משערין לשהיית שחיטת בהמה, ובכדי שחיטת עוף אחר משערינן לשהיית שחיטת עוף:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:6:1.english: An animal for an animal, and a bird for a bird - The time it takes to slaughter another animal is what we use to estimate the [permissible] delay in the slaughtering of an animal, and the time it takes to slaughter another bird is what we use to estimate the delay in the slaughtering of a bird.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:6:2.hebrew: או דילמא אפילו - בכדי שחיטת בהמה משערינן לשהיית שחיטת העוף, דהיינו קולא:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:6:2.english: Or perhaps even - We measure the time of delay [that invalidates the slaughter] of a bird by the time it takes to slaughter an animal, which is a leniency.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:7:1.english: He said to them: I was not at ease with my beloved [uncle], that I could ask him - I was not overly familiar with my uncle Rabbi Chiyya when I studied this halakha, and he did not have a cheerful countenance toward me, such that I could ask him about this matter. Rav was the son of Rabbi Chiyya's brother and the son of his sister.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:8:1.hebrew: אף בהמה לעוף - קולא היא שנתנו לעוף שיעור שחיטת בהמה לשהייתו:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:8:1.english: Also [the time of] an animal for a bird - This is a leniency, that they gave a bird the measure of an animal's slaughtering for its [permitted] delay.

Rashi on Chullin 32a:9:1.hebrew: לשיעורין - פעמים שהיא רחוקה ופעמים קרובה:
Rashi on Chullin 32a:9:1.english: In increments - [I.e., the amount of time it takes to bring another animal is not fixed,] for sometimes it is far and sometimes near.

Tosafot on Chullin 32a:16:1.hebrew: כדי ביקור טבח חכם - ובסכין הראוייה לאותה בהמה, חוץ לצואר כמלא צואר:
Tosafot on Chullin 32a:16:1.english: As long as an expert slaughterer's examination - and with a knife suited to that animal, [examining] beyond the neck an area equal to the full [width of the] neck.

Tosafot on Chullin 32a:19:1.hebrew: ורמינהי אלו טרפות בבהמה פסוקת הגרגרת - וא"ת: נהי דנבלה הויא, מ"מ לא פקע מינה איסור טרפות, וחייב אף משום טריפות, כדמשמע בשמעתין דמסוכנת (לקמן חולין לז.). והא דאמר בפרק חטאת העוף (זבחים דף סט:) יצא עוף טמא שאין במינו טרפה - לא משום דלא שייכא ביה שחיטה, ואפילו נשחטה הויא נבלה, ופקע מינה איסור טרפה כי אתא איסור נבלה; אלא פירוש שאין במינו טרפה, היינו טרפה לחודיה, דאף כי נשחט לקי אף משום נבלה. וי"ל דהכי פריך: דאי איתא דלא מהניא ביה שחיטה והויא ליה נבלה, לא הוה ליה למיתני אלו טרפות, אלא הוה ליה למיתני ואלו נבלות, שהוא עיקר האיסור. ואם תאמר דנקט איסור טרפה לאשמועינן שאם חתך כזית בשר מחיים, דלקי אף משום טרפה. ויש לומר דמתניתין דאלו טרפות משמע ליה לאחר שחיטה, מדקתני סיפא כל שאין כמוה חיה, ולא קתני כל שאין חיה:
Tosafot on Chullin 32a:19:1.english: And we raise a contradiction: these are [the cases of] tereifah in an animal: one whose trachea is severed - And if you say: granted that it becomes a neveilah, nevertheless the prohibition of tereifah does not depart from it, and he is liable also on account of tereifah, as is implied in our sugya regarding a dying animal (mesukenet) (below, Chullin 37a). And as for that which is stated in the chapter "Chatat Ha'Of" (Zevachim 69b), "this excludes an impure bird, which has no tereifah in its species" - [this is] not because shechitah is inapplicable to it, [such] that even if it were slaughtered it would be a neveilah, and the prohibition of tereifah would depart from it once the prohibition of neveilah took effect; rather, the meaning of "which has no tereifah in its species" is that it has no tereifah alone, for even when it is slaughtered [in the manner that would constitute tereifah], it is liable also on account of neveilah. And one can say that this is the force of the question: for if it were so that shechitah does not avail for it and it becomes a neveilah, [the mishnah] should not have taught "these are tereifot," but rather it should have taught "and these are nevelot," since that is the primary prohibition. And if you say [that the mishnah] used [the term] "tereifah" in order to teach us that if one cut an olive's-bulk of flesh [from the animal] while it was alive, he is liable also on account of tereifah - one can say that the mishnah of "these are tereifot" is understood [by the Gemara] to be [discussing a case] after shechitah, since it teaches in the latter clause, "anything the like of which cannot live," and does not teach, "anything that cannot live."

Tosafot on Chullin 32a:1:1.hebrew: נשחטה בהמה אחרת עמה לרבנן פרה כשרה - ואם תאמר: ואותה ולא אותה וחבירתה לרבנן למה לי? אי לשוחט בהמה אחרת עמה, תיפוק ליה מטעם מלאכה, כמו חתך דלעת עמה. ויש לומר דאיצטריך לשוחט שתי פרות ונתכוין לשחוט, דמשום מלאכה אחרת לא מפסלו, כיון דשתיהן לשם פרה:
Tosafot on Chullin 32a:1:1.english: If another animal was slaughtered together with it, according to the Rabbis the cow is valid - And if you should say: [the exclusion of] "her" - and not her and her companion (i.e., two together) - why do I need this according to the Rabbis? If [it comes to teach about] one who slaughters another animal with it, let this be derived from the reason of [extraneous] labor, just as [in the case of] one who cut a gourd with it [during the slaughter, which invalidates it]. And one can say that it is needed for [the case of] one who slaughters two cows and intends [both] slaughterings, for [in that case] they are not invalidated on account of "another labor", since both are for the sake of a [red] cow.

Tosafot on Chullin 32a:2:1.hebrew: אבל פרה דחולין אימא לא קמ"ל - וא"ת: דאמר בריש זבחים (דף ז.) שחט אחת על מי שמחוייב חטאת פסולה, על מי שמחוייב עולה כשרה, דכתיב וכפר עליו ולא על חבירו, חבירו דומיא דידיה שמחוייב חטאת כמותו; והכא נמי נימא אותה ולא אותה, וחבירתה דומיא דידה. ויש לומר, דהתם וכפר עליו משמע עליו מכפר ולא על חבירו מכפר, על המחוייב חטאת כזה דשייכא ביה כפרה זו:
Tosafot on Chullin 32a:2:1.english: But an ordinary (non-consecrated) cow, you might say [Rabbi Natan] would not need to teach us [this] - And you might ask: it is stated at the beginning of [tractate] Zevachim (7a) [that] if one slaughtered a single [animal, intending it] on behalf of one who is liable for a chatat (sin-offering), it is invalid; on behalf of one who is liable for an olah (burnt-offering), it is valid, since it is written, "and he shall atone for him" - and not for his fellow; his fellow being comparable to him, [meaning] one who is liable for a chatat like him. And here too, let us say [likewise, that the verse implies] "her" and not "her" - her fellow being comparable to her [i.e., another parah, so that slaughtering one on behalf of another parah should equally be invalid, making Rabbi Natan's teaching superfluous]. And one can say: that there, "and he shall atone for him" implies [that] he atones for him, and not for his fellow does he atone - [namely,] for one who is liable for a chatat such as this one, to whom this atonement is relevant [i.e., that exclusion is tied to the atonement-verse itself, which does not apply in the same way to the parah, so Rabbi Natan's teaching is still necessary].

Tosafot on Chullin 32a:8:1.hebrew: ושמואל אמר אף בהמה לעוף - ר"ח פסק כשמואל ורבי יוחנן דאמרי בהמה לעוף, ובקונטרס פסק לחומרא כרב דאמר עוף לעוף, דקיימי אמוראי דמערבא כוותיה, דאמרי דקה לדקה וגסה לגסה, וכ"ש עוף לעוף, דיותר חלוק עוף מבהמה ממה שחלוקין דקה מגסה. וגם בה"ג פסק גסה לגסה ודקה לדקה ועוף לעוף:
Tosafot on Chullin 32a:8:1.english: And Shmuel said: Even an animal for a bird - Rabbeinu Chananel ruled like Shmuel and Rabbi Yochanan, who say [the measure of time is that of slaughtering] an animal for a bird. And in the Kuntres (Rashi), he ruled stringently like Rav, who says [the measure is that of] a bird for a bird, for the amoraim of the West (Eretz Yisrael) hold like him, who say [the measure for] small animals [is that of] small animals and [for] large animals [is that of] large animals, and all the more so [for] a bird, [the measure is that of] a bird, for a bird is more distinct from an animal than small animals are distinct from large animals. And also the Ba'al Halakhot Gedolot ruled: large for large, small for small, and bird for bird.
